newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela privatization plans run into opposition.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela privatization plans run into opposition.

text.p: High-ranking legislators from various Venezuelan political parties harshly criticized Tuesday the government's privatization program and called for an in-depth debate of the sale of state companies.

Government plans to sell off state assets in the aluminum and steel sectors, set for the first half of 1997, were singled out for particular criticism during a hearing of the Chamber of Deputies Energy and Mines Committee.
The legislators made their comments to Elias Ynaty, president of the state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) which groups together the companies due to be privatized.
Carmelo Lauria, deputy with largest opposition party Democratic Action (AD) accused the government of trying "to push through the privatizations for reasons of international vanity."

Government officials have said they hope to raise at least $3 billion from the sale of steel company Sidor, ferro silica company Fesilven, aluminum smelters Alcasa and Venalum, bauxite producer Bauxilum and carbon anode producer Carbonorca.
Deputy Henry Ramos Allup, head of the AD faction in Congress, said that in Venezuela "the disastrous privatization process has been used merely to liquidate assets and not as a development policy."
Ramos also criticized the government's plans to sell state companies to large international consortiums. "We are leaving a state monopoly to become a private international monopoly."
Legislators from social Christian party Copei and union based Radical Cause added their support to a call for the privatization of the basic industries to be debated in depth.
"Congress has the last word," said Copei deputy Ramon Jose Medina who noted that there were many unresolved issues surrounding the sell-off plans.
